sn22.31:1.2: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you misery and the root of misery.
sn22.31:1.5: Form is misery; feeling is misery; perception is misery; volitional formations are misery; consciousness is misery.
sn22.31:1.7: “And what, bhikkhus, is the root of misery?
sn22.31:1.8: It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, seeking delight here and there; that is,
sn22.31:1.9: craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for extermination.
sn22.31:1.10: This is called the root of misery.”
